steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Latent Lattice Language Models
summary: The Lattice replaces the standard Transformer residual stream (and the internal states of SSM/linear-attention hybrids) by adding persistent per-layer horizontal latent streams that directly condition attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. It requires training from scratch with increased architectural complexity and a larger state footprint than parameter-matched baselines, though exact inference latency and memory costs are not quantified in the abstract. Adoption can fail because benefits are demonstrated only at the 406M scale on 20B tokens, and the recurrent latents may introduce unforeseen training instabilities or deployment overheads that negate perplexity gains at production scale.
rationale: The technique requires training foundation models from scratch and validating recurrent state dynamics at scale, which exceeds the reader's constrained infrastructure and budget.
technique: Lattice of Latents (persistent per-layer latent streams)

claims.statement: The Lattice replaces the standard Transformer residual stream (and the internal states of SSM/linear-attention hybrids) by adding persistent per-layer horizontal latent streams that directly condition attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. It requires training from scratch with increased architectural complexity and a larger state footprint than parameter-matched baselines, though exact inference latency and memory costs are not quantified in the abstract. Adoption can fail because benefits are demonstrated only at the 406M scale on 20B tokens, and the recurrent latents may introduce unforeseen training instabilities or deployment overheads that negate perplexity gains at production scale.

On Transformers trained on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, a 406M-parameter Lattice model lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 to 14.40 over a parameter-matched Transformer; with hyper-connections and input residuals, it lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 (base) and 14.22 (enhanced Transformer) to 13.61.
